## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-12-build-gene-co-expression-networks-using-hdwgcna/>

Part 1 of 2. hdWGCNA adapts weighted gene co-expression network analysis
(WGCNA) to single-cell data. Single cells are too sparse for correlation
networks, so cells of one type from one sample are first aggregated into
**metacells** (a cell and its nearest neighbors); the network is then built on
the metacell expression of a single cell type (here `params$target.celltype`).

This notebook: loads the downsampled annotated Seurat object, initializes
hdWGCNA, builds and normalizes metacells, sets the expression data for the
target cell type, and scans soft-thresholding powers. The power table is
printed so that `soft.power` can be chosen in part 2 (manual decision). Part 2
constructs the network, module eigengenes, hub genes, enrichment and
differential module analysis.

**Input:** the object `seurat_subset_downsampled.rds` is created by
`scRNAseq_tutorial_7_trajectory_monocle3/tut7_trajectory_monocle3_part1.Rmd`,
which must be run first (the article calls it `seurat_subset.rds`).

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 1-5). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments. Note: the article's step headings are partly mislabelled
(several code blocks sit under the previous step's heading and there is no
"Step 9" code block); the `# STEP` banners here follow the article's h2/h3
headings.

## Libraries and data

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load Libraries and Data
#-----------------------------------------------
library(hdWGCNA)
library(WGCNA)
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(patchwork)
library(igraph)
library(enrichR)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Directories (the article uses setwd() and relative paths)
base.dir <- params$base.dir
wgcna.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$wgcna.subdir)

# Create output directory for all saved plots (and results)
for (d in c("plots", "results")) {
  dir.create(file.path(wgcna.dir, d), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

set.seed(params$seed)

# Column names from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
target.celltype <- params$target.celltype

# Enable multi-threading for WGCNA correlation computations
# Use the number of CPU cores available on your machine
enableWGCNAThreads(nThreads = params$n.threads)

# Load the downsampled annotated Seurat object saved in Part 7 (tutorial 7, part 1)
input.path <- file.path(base.dir, params$input.subdir, params$input.rds)
# ADDED: clear error if tutorial 7 part 1 has not been run
if (!file.exists(input.path)) {
  stop("Input object not found: ", input.path,
       "\nRun tut7_trajectory_monocle3_part1.Rmd first.")
}
seurat_obj <- readRDS(input.path)

# Confirm key metadata columns are present
colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)
# ADDED: stop early if a needed metadata column is missing
stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, sample.col, condition.col) %in%
                colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)))

print(table(seurat_obj[[celltype.col]][, 1]))
print(table(seurat_obj[[condition.col]][, 1]))

# ADDED: the target cell type must be present
celltype.labels <- unique(as.character(seurat_obj[[celltype.col]][, 1]))
if (!target.celltype %in% celltype.labels) {
  stop("target.celltype '", target.celltype, "' not found in ", celltype.col,
       ". Available labels: ", paste(sort(celltype.labels), collapse = ", "))
}

# ADDED: the reductions used for metacells (part 1) and plots (part 2) must exist
stopifnot(params$metacell.reduction %in% Reductions(seurat_obj),
          params$umap.reduction %in% Reductions(seurat_obj))

# ADDED: metacells are built per cell type x sample; the article groups by
# orig.ident, which must identify the biological sample
if (sample.col == "orig.ident" && "sample_id" %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)) {
  n.orig <- length(unique(seurat_obj$orig.ident))
  n.sample <- length(unique(seurat_obj$sample_id))
  if (n.orig < n.sample) {
    warning("orig.ident has ", n.orig, " levels but sample_id has ", n.sample,
            "; orig.ident is not per-sample. Consider sample.col = 'sample_id'.")
  }
}
```

## Initialize hdWGCNA

```{r step2_setup}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Initialize hdWGCNA with SetupForWGCNA
#-----------------------------------------------
seurat_obj <- SetupForWGCNA(
  seurat_obj,
  gene_select = params$gene.select,   # Include genes expressed in at least 'fraction' of cells
  fraction    = params$gene.fraction, # 5% minimum cell fraction -- filters very rare transcripts
  wgcna_name  = params$wgcna.name     # Label for this analysis instance inside the Seurat object
)
```

## Construct metacells

```{r step3_metacells}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Construct Metacells
#-----------------------------------------------
seurat_obj <- MetacellsByGroups(
  seurat_obj  = seurat_obj,
  group.by    = c(celltype.col, sample.col), # Never mix cell types or samples
  k           = params$metacell.k,           # Aggregate the 20 nearest neighbors into each metacell
  max_shared  = params$metacell.max_shared,  # Max cells shared between any two metacells (controls overlap)
  reduction   = params$metacell.reduction,   # Use CCA integration embeddings for nearest-neighbor search
  ident.group = celltype.col
)

# Normalize the metacell expression matrix
seurat_obj <- NormalizeMetacells(seurat_obj)
```

## Set the expression data

```{r step4_datexpr}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Set the Expression Data for Network Construction
#-----------------------------------------------
seurat_obj <- SetDatExpr(
  seurat_obj,
  group_name = target.celltype,     # The cell type to analyze
  group.by   = celltype.col,        # Metadata column containing cell type labels
  assay      = params$expr.assay,
  slot       = params$expr.slot     # Use log-normalized expression
)
```

## Select the soft-thresholding power

```{r step5_softpower}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Select the Soft-Thresholding Power
#-----------------------------------------------
# Test a range of soft powers (1-20 for signed networks)
seurat_obj <- TestSoftPowers(seurat_obj, networkType = params$network.type)

# Assigning to a variable avoids any attempt to render on screen (important on HPC)
plot_list <- PlotSoftPowers(seurat_obj)
p_softpower <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = params$powers.ncol)
ggsave(file.path(wgcna.dir, "plots/soft_power.pdf"), plot = p_softpower, width = 10, height = 5)
# ADDED: show the plot in the notebook
print(p_softpower)

# ADDED: print the power table to guide the choice of soft.power (part 2);
# pick the lowest power at which the scale-free fit (SFT.R.sq) reaches ~0.8-0.9
power_table <- GetPowerTable(seurat_obj)
print(power_table)
```

The soft power itself is chosen in part 2 (`params$soft.power`, article default
6) after inspecting the plot and table above.

## Save objects for part 2

```{r step5_save}
# ADDED: hand-off to part 2 (hdWGCNA results live inside the Seurat object)
saveRDS(seurat_obj, file.path(wgcna.dir, "results/seurat_wgcna_prenetwork.rds"))
```
